Subject: Ilya Sokolov — quick debrief request + ownership matrix

Team —

Thanks for meeting with Ilya yesterday. Fast ask: please drop your numeric score (1-10), 2–3 sentence rationale, and one explicit gap (if any) by EOD PT today. Recruiting needs a final pass by tomorrow so we can decide whether to move to an offer.

Key context: this is for Staff SWE, systems-heavy role (KV cache / serving runtime). Candidate has strong infra background but skipped on a couple of design tradeoffs. I'm trying to capture a small ownership matrix (who will own the final tiebreak items) so we don't get stuck.

Scorecard link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-ilya-scorecard (please add a 1-line vote at the top)
Attachment: Ilya_Sokolov_scorecard.pdf (interview notes + recordings stub)

Proposed ownership matrix (suggested):
- System design concerns: Ava
- Performance/latency tradeoffs (kernel selection): Marissa
- Offer/comp recommendation: Ben + Recruiting

If you think a 10–15m sync would help, ping availability — otherwise reply-all with your votes.

Ben

Sr. Eng Manager, Infra
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ilya Sokolov — quick debrief request + ownership matrix

Ben / team —

Vote: YES — 8/10
Rationale: Really solid systems intuition and debugging flow. In the design exercise he proposed an elegant KV eviction heuristic and demonstrated awareness of cache-warmup behaviors on cold starts. His performance numbers (from the take-home and interview walkthrough) were believable and he'd be straightforward to pair with for kernel-level optimizations.

Primary gap: less experience with multi-tenant routing policies and the posture around graceful degradation. He described fallbacks in theory but wasn't specific about request-routing strategies under resource pressure. That's my item to own for a follow-up question set if we move forward.

Notes attached: marissa_notes_0903.txt (short bullets)

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Ben / Marissa —

Vote: NO — 5/10
Rationale: Strong coding and systems chops on a single-node scale; I'd be concerned about his approach to KV cache coherence across sharded hosts. In the system design he favored asymmetric sharding to avoid cross-node coordination but glossed over how he'd handle rebalances and tail latency spikes. For a Staff role that will own inter-node reliability, that matters.

Primary gap: cross-shard coordination & observability (logs/metrics design). I attached a quick sketch (ava_design_snippets.png) with the specific points I want a follow-up on. If we had a short (15m) follow-up focused on rebalancing strategy and an instrumentation plan, that could resolve most concerns.

I'm happy to own the design follow-up. If Marissa is comfortable driving the performance questions we can converge.

—Ava
